subject.title: [Bug] Gateway swallows user-visible reply when an agent's exec stdout matches "configuration file" — replies=2 puts ⚠️ 🛠️ first, the actual reply second

question: Should successful agent turns with recovered or ambiguous exec/tool errors show a user-visible channel warning, and if so should that warning be suppressed, inline, or ordered before the final answer?
rationale: Current tests and docs intentionally keep mutating-tool warnings visible by default, while this report shows that default can make users believe the real reply was lost; automation should not choose that UX/security tradeoff without maintainer intent.

options.title: Define recovered-warning policy
options.body: Prefer a shared rule that suppresses or inline-demotes non-terminal/recovered warnings after a successful visible reply, with Feishu and shared payload regression proof.

options.title: Keep current safety warning default
options.body: Treat the extra warning as intentional for mutating-tool safety and route operators to `messages.suppressToolErrors` or the broader configuration request.

options.title: Split remaining work by canonical areas
options.body: Track Feishu visual ordering, Codex/native false positives, and global warning policy separately, then close this issue only after its unique Feishu evidence is represented there.

recommendation.title: Define recovered-warning policy
recommendation.body: Prefer a shared rule that suppresses or inline-demotes non-terminal/recovered warnings after a successful visible reply, with Feishu and shared payload regression proof.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the Feishu answer-preservation fix and has recent history in the Codex/agent delivery boundary touched by this policy choice.
